items.followUp: Differentiate between grana and stroma in a chloroplast.

rubric.why: Thylakoids are flattened membrane sacs that contain chlorophyll.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying thylakoids as flattened sacs or chlorophyll-containing structures.

rubric.why: The stroma is the chloroplast’s fluid matrix and contains enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the stroma as the fluid matrix or noting that it contains enzymes.

modelAnswer: Thylakoids are flattened membrane sacs containing chlorophyll; they are arranged in stacks called grana.
The stroma is the fluid matrix of the chloroplast, containing enzymes, in which the grana are embedded.

items.followUp: How does a light microscope differ from an electron microscope?

rubric.why: A TEM passes electrons through a thin specimen to reveal internal details.
rubric.description: Explains how a TEM forms an image.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons pass through a thin specimen and show its internal structure.

rubric.why: An SEM scans the specimen’s surface to show its surface structure.
rubric.description: Explains how an SEM forms an image.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an SEM scans the specimen’s surface.

modelAnswer: A transmission electron microscope (TEM) passes electrons through a thin specimen and shows its internal details.
A scanning electron microscope (SEM) scans the specimen’s surface and shows its surface details, usually as a three-dimensional image.

items.followUp: Describe how a cell plate forms during cytokinesis in a plant cell.

rubric.why: The phragmoplast guides the formation of the cell plate between the daughter nuclei.
rubric.description: States the role or location of the cell plate during cytokinesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the phragmoplast guides cell-plate formation or that the plate forms between the daughter nuclei.

rubric.why: The cell plate develops into a new cell wall that separates the daughter cells.
rubric.description: States the outcome of cell-plate formation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cell plate forms a new wall or separates the daughter cells.

modelAnswer: The phragmoplast guides the formation of the cell plate between the daughter nuclei.
The cell plate grows outwards and develops into a new cell wall, separating the two daughter cells.

items.followUp: Give one example of a diploid cell and one example of a haploid cell.

rubric.why: Body or somatic cells are examples of diploid cells.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a diploid cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a body or somatic cell as diploid.

rubric.why: Gametes, such as sperm or egg cells, are examples of haploid cells.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a haploid cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a gamete, sperm, egg or ovum as haploid.

modelAnswer: A gamete, such as a sperm or egg cell, is haploid (n).
